# claude-skills, Codex distribution

This directory is a Codex-compatible build of the claude-skills catalog. It is
generated by `scripts/build-codex.mjs` from the repo's `skills/` source and is
safe to regenerate at any time (the build is idempotent and reversible).

## Quickstart

### 1. Install into a project

Run this in the project root:

```
npx degit rampstackco/claude-skills/dist/codex/.agents .agents
```

It copies the catalog into `.agents/skills/`, one folder per skill. Codex scans
`.agents/skills` in every directory from where you launch it up to the
repository root, so the skills are available anywhere inside the project.

### 2. Or install for your user

To make the skills available in every project, install them into the user
skills folder instead:

```
npx degit rampstackco/claude-skills/dist/codex/.agents/skills "$HOME/.agents/skills" --force
```

`$HOME/.agents/skills` is the user location in the
[Codex skills documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills).
`--force` is needed when that folder already exists; it writes the catalog's
skill folders and leaves other skills in the folder in place.

### 3. Mind the description budget

Codex lists every installed skill's name and description inside a fixed budget,
`skills.max_context_tokens`, and shortens descriptions to fit. With the full
catalog installed and the default budget of 5440, Codex cut every description to
about 535 characters, and 88 of the 103 descriptions run longer than that. What
survives is the front of each description: what the skill does and its trigger
phrases. The yield clauses that send a request to a sibling skill come later, so
they are cut. Measured on `codex-cli 0.154.0-alpha.6.2`; the log lines are cited
in [`PORT_NOTES.md`](PORT_NOTES.md).

Two ways to give descriptions more room:

- **Install only the skills you need (recommended).** Fewer skills share the
  budget. Copy each skill's folder from this distribution. For one skill, run
  this in the project root:

  ```
  npx degit rampstackco/claude-skills/dist/codex/.agents/skills/creative-brief .agents/skills/creative-brief
  ```

  Repeat it for each skill you want, with the skill's name in both places. Each
  run lands one folder holding that skill's `SKILL.md` and its `references/`.

  The curated subset repos
  ([starter](https://github.com/rampstackco/claude-skills-starter),
  [seo](https://github.com/rampstackco/claude-skills-seo), and
  [pm](https://github.com/rampstackco/claude-skills-pm)) ship Claude's layout
  without a Codex build and are untested in Codex, so they are not recommended
  for Codex until they carry a `dist/codex`.

- **Raise the budget (secondary).** In `config.toml`:

  ```toml
  [skills]
  max_context_tokens = 10000
  ```

  The [configuration reference](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference)
  caps the setting at 10,000. Tested value: none yet. No run has changed the
  setting, so how much description text a higher value keeps is not measured.

### 4. What loads

- 103 skills and 490 reference files, under `.agents/skills/<name>/`.
- All three disclosure tiers were observed loading in the Codex desktop app on
  2026-09-15: each skill's name and description, its `SKILL.md` body, and its
  `references/` files. The body and reference reads come from the app session's
  reported tool history, recorded in [`PORT_NOTES.md`](PORT_NOTES.md).

### 5. MCP servers

Some skills call MCP servers; the SEO audit suite uses the Ahrefs MCP.
`agents/openai.yaml` is a commented template listing every server the build
detected. The operator supplies the real server URLs, names, and auth; nothing
in the template is live.

### 6. Scope

The catalog installs and loads in Codex. No performance claim is made, and the
served model was not independently attested.

## What this is

- `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for all 103 skills, with frontmatter
  normalized to the portable core (`name` + `description` only).
- `.agents/skills/<name>/references/` carried over byte for byte, plus a
  `_claude-frontmatter-extras.yaml` sidecar holding the Claude-only metadata
  (`category`, `catalog_summary`, `display_order`) so the port stays reversible.
- `agents/openai.yaml`: the commented MCP wiring template described above.

See `PORT_NOTES.md` for the full feasibility writeup, frontmatter rationale, and
caveats.

## Regenerate

From the repo root:

```
node scripts/build-codex.mjs
```

The script prints a transform log (skills copied, reference files copied,
frontmatter keys sidecar'd, longest description and its headroom under the Codex
cap, MCP refs detected) followed by a validation pass with PASS/FAIL per check.

Two read-only modes back the CI drift guard, and are what
`.github/workflows/dist-drift.yml` runs on every PR that can invalidate this
tree:

```
node scripts/build-codex.mjs --check      # committed tree vs a fresh rebuild
node scripts/build-codex.mjs --validate   # validate the committed tree in place
```
